I read all 76 lines and every proof in the file. The five theorems form a layered chain.

1. `map_noise_restrict_atom` is the only proof that contains independence reasoning. It uses `measure_inter_preimage_eq_mul`.
2. `map_observation_restrict_atom` reduces to (1). It replaces `T (X ω)` by `T x` almost everywhere on the atom, then uses `map_map` and `map_smul`.
3. `map_observation_restrict_atom_of_hasLaw` is a one-line rewrite of (2) with `hρ.map_eq`.
4. `map_observation_restrict_atom_withDensity` rewrites (3) and applies `withDensity_smul`.
5. `map_observation_restrict_atom_withDensity_ofReal` calls (4) and then does a short `ofReal`/`toReal` computation.

Each theorem calls its predecessor instead of repeating its argument. The leftover blocks are short rewrites and routine `ENNReal` conversions. The rubric excludes these, along with thin wrappers. I found no nontrivial reasoning duplicated across two or more proofs in this file. I did not search the rest of the repository for similar blocks in other files, because the rubric asks for repetition across proofs and I found none to cite here.
